userStories.title: Store read side — entry id and detailed read
acceptanceCriteria: `approvalId(entry)` returns a string of exactly 8 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
`approvalId` returns the same value for two entries whose `stage`, `command` and `approvedAt` are identical.
`approvalId` returns different values for two entries with the same `stage` and `command` but different `approvedAt`.
`approvalId(entry)` equals the first 8 hex characters of the SHA-256 digest of `stage + "\0" + command + "\0" + approvedAt`.
`approvalId` on an entry whose `approvedAt` is missing returns the value computed with `approvedAt` as `""`.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed(path)` on a path with no file resolves to a value deep-equal to `{ state: "missing", file: { entries: [], taint: undefined }, droppedMalformed: 0 }`.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file whose content is not valid JSON returns `state: "unparseable"`.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file whose top-level JSON value is an array returns `state: "unparseable"`.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file whose `entries` value is a string returns `state: "unparseable"`.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file whose content is not valid JSON returns `file` deep-equal to `{ entries: [], taint: undefined }`.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file holding two valid entries and one `null` element returns `state: "ok"`.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file holding two valid entries and one `null` element returns `file.entries` deep-equal to the two valid entries.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file holding two valid entries and one `null` element returns `droppedMalformed: 1`.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file whose `taint` is `{ since: "s", runId: "r", pid: 7 }` returns `file.taint` deep-equal to that object.
`readApprovalsFile(path)` on a valid tainted file returns a value deep-equal to `readApprovalsFileDetailed(path).file`.
`readApprovalsFile(path)` on a file whose `entries` value is a string returns an empty `entries` array.
`readApprovalsFileDetailed` on a file whose `entries` value is a string and whose `taint` is `{ since: "s", runId: "r", pid: 7 }` returns `file.taint` deep-equal to that object.

routing.reasoning: Approval cache integrity and derived cryptographic identifiers are security-critical; retain legacy cache behavior.

userStories.title: Store removal — removeApprovals
acceptanceCriteria: `removeApprovals` on a path with no file resolves to `{ outcome: "unchanged" }`.
After `removeApprovals` on a path with no file, no file exists at that path.
`removeApprovals` on a path with no file invokes `decide` once with a read whose `state` is `"missing"`.
`removeApprovals` on an unparseable file resolves to `{ outcome: "refused", reason: "approvals.json could not be parsed; not rewriting it" }`.
After `removeApprovals` on an unparseable file, the file's bytes are unchanged.
`removeApprovals` on an unparseable file does not invoke `decide`.
`removeApprovals` whose `decide` returns `{ refuse: "Unknown id(s): deadbeef" }` resolves to `{ outcome: "refused", reason: "Unknown id(s): deadbeef" }`.
After `removeApprovals` whose `decide` returns a `refuse`, the file's bytes are unchanged.
`removeApprovals` whose `remove` predicate selects no entry resolves to `{ outcome: "unchanged" }`.
After `removeApprovals` whose `remove` predicate selects no entry, the file's bytes are unchanged.
`removeApprovals` whose `remove` predicate selects one of three entries resolves with `removed` deep-equal to that one entry.
After `removeApprovals` removes one of three entries, `readApprovals(path)` returns exactly the other two entries.
After `removeApprovals` removes an entry from a tainted store, `readApprovalsFile(path).taint` deep-equals the taint read before the call.
After `removeApprovals` removes an entry from an untainted store, `readApprovalsFile(path).taint` is `undefined`.
`removeApprovals` removing an entry from a file that also holds one malformed element resolves with `droppedMalformed: 1`.

Given a store holding only entry A, when `removeApprovals` selecting A and `appendApproval` adding entry B are started concurrently on the same path, `readApprovals(path)` after both settle deep-equals `[B]`.

routing.reasoning: Access revocation and taint-preserving concurrent store writes are security-critical.

userStories.title: nax approvals list — store states and JSON
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete listing of missing, corrupt and partly malformed stores and machine-readable JSON output.

**Motivation** — Operators need to see whether the approvals cache is currently trusted or tainted and audit remembered grants.

**Approach** — For a missing store, stdout `No remembered approvals at <path>` and exit 0. For an unparseable store, stderr `approvals.json could not be parsed; the cache reads it as empty`, stdout `No remembered approvals at <path>` (or the JSON body with `--json`), exit 0. For malformed elements, stderr `<n> malformed entries ignored` and continue listing valid entries. `list --json` prints one JSON object on stdout with `path`, `state`, `taint` (null when absent), `droppedMalformed` and `entries`, each entry `{ id: approvalId(entry), ...entry }`; for a store whose content is not valid JSON output `{ path, state: "unparseable", taint: null, droppedMalformed: 0, entries: [] }` while keeping the parse warning on stderr. Add `--json` to the `### nax approvals list` documentation.

**Scope** — In: list states, warning and JSON formatting. Out: human output already supplied by US-003, removal by id/stage (US-005), all/confirmation (US-006).

**Interface**
```ts
export function toListJson(path: string, read: ApprovalsFileRead): object;   // the `--json` body
export async function approvalsListCommand(opts: { workdir: string; json: boolean }, deps?: typeof _approvalsCliDeps): Promise<number>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: `approvalsListCommand` on a missing store writes `No remembered approvals at <path>` to stdout.
`approvalsListCommand` on a missing store resolves to `0`.
`approvalsListCommand` on an unparseable store writes `approvals.json could not be parsed; the cache reads it as empty` to stderr.
`approvalsListCommand` on an unparseable store writes `No remembered approvals at <path>` to stdout.
`approvalsListCommand` on an unparseable store resolves to `0`.
`approvalsListCommand` on a store with 1 malformed element writes `1 malformed entries ignored` to stderr.
`approvalsListCommand` on a store with 1 malformed element and 1 valid entry writes the valid entry's first line to stdout.
`approvalsListCommand` with `json: true` writes to stdout exactly one JSON object whose keys are `path`, `state`, `taint`, `droppedMalformed` and `entries`.
`approvalsListCommand` with `json: true` writes each element of `entries` deep-equal to `{ id: approvalId(entry), ...entry }`.
`approvalsListCommand` with `json: true` on an untainted store writes `taint` as `null`.
`approvalsListCommand` with `json: true` on a tainted store writes `taint` deep-equal to the store's taint.
`approvalsListCommand` with `json: true` on a missing store writes `state` as `"missing"`.
`approvalsListCommand` with `json: true` on a missing store writes `entries` as an empty array.

`approvalsListCommand` with `json: true` on a store whose content is not valid JSON writes a stdout JSON object deep-equal to `{ path, state: "unparseable", taint: null, droppedMalformed: 0, entries: [] }`.
`approvalsListCommand` with `json: true` on an unparseable store writes `approvals.json could not be parsed; the cache reads it as empty` to stderr.

routing.reasoning: Exposes access-control and taint state; security override applies despite straightforward formatting.

userStories.title: nax approvals rm --all and store failure mapping
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Finish guarded full revocation and translate store failures into actionable CLI messages.

**Motivation** — Operators need a safe way to revoke all remembered grants without accidentally enabling a tainted cache.

**Approach** — `nax approvals rm --all [--yes] [-d <dir>]` asks `promptForConfirmation` unless `--yes` is given; without a TTY and without `--yes` it refuses without prompting. An empty or missing store is reported before any prompt: stdout `No remembered approvals at <path>`, exit 0, no write. Declined confirmation or non-TTY without `--yes`: stderr `Aborted`, exit 1, no write. An unparseable store on rm: stderr `approvals.json could not be parsed; not rewriting it`, exit 1, file untouched. Malformed elements dropped by a rewrite: stderr `<n> malformed entries dropped`. `FILE_LOCK_TIMEOUT`: stderr `a nax run is writing <path>; retry`, exit 1. Any other store error: stderr `Failed to update <path>: <message>`, exit 1. Add a `### nax approvals rm` section to `docs/guides/cli-reference.md`, and add one sentence to `docs/adr/ADR-030-bash-approval-modes.md` ("The approvals cache's trust boundary") saying grants are listed and revoked with `nax approvals`, which never clears a taint. stdout is for removal confirmations/nothing-there; stderr for warnings, usage errors, `Aborted` and failures. Only a trusted run clears taint through `clearApprovalsTaint` (unchanged).

**Scope** — In: `--all` confirmation, empty-store precheck, rm error/warning mapping and docs. Out: selector basics and ID/stage removal (US-005), clearing or rewriting the approvals `taint` marker from the CLI.

**Interface**
```ts
export async function approvalsRmCommand(
  opts: { workdir: string; ids: readonly string[]; stage?: string; all: boolean; yes: boolean },
  deps?: typeof _approvalsCliDeps,
): Promise<number>;
```

**Verification** — Manual smoke: `bun bin/nax.ts approvals rm --all --yes -d <temp project>`.
acceptanceCriteria: After `approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: true`, `readApprovals(path)` returns an empty array.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: true` does not invoke `deps.confirm`.
After `approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: false` on a TTY whose `deps.confirm` resolves `true`, `readApprovals(path)` returns an empty array.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: false` on a TTY whose `deps.confirm` resolves `false` resolves to `1`.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: false` on a TTY whose `deps.confirm` resolves `false` writes `Aborted` to stderr.
After `approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: false` on a TTY whose `deps.confirm` resolves `false`, the store file's bytes are unchanged.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: false` when `deps.isTTY()` is false resolves to `1`.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: false` when `deps.isTTY()` is false writes `Aborted` to stderr.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: false` when `deps.isTTY()` is false does not invoke `deps.confirm`.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true` on a missing store writes `No remembered approvals at <path>` to stdout.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true` on a missing store resolves to `0`.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true` on a missing store does not invoke `deps.confirm`.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true` on an existing store whose `entries` is empty writes `No remembered approvals at <path>` to stdout.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true` on an existing store whose `entries` is empty resolves to `0`.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true` on an existing store whose `entries` is empty does not invoke `deps.confirm`.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: true` on an unparseable store resolves to `1`.
`approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: true` on an unparseable store writes `approvals.json could not be parsed; not rewriting it` to stderr.
After `approvalsRmCommand` with `all: true, yes: true` on an unparseable store, the store file's bytes are unchanged.
`approvalsRmCommand` whose removal drops 1 malformed element writes `1 malformed entries dropped` to stderr.
`approvalsRmCommand` whose `deps.removeApprovals` rejects with a `NaxError` of code `FILE_LOCK_TIMEOUT` resolves to `1`.

`approvalsRmCommand` whose `deps.removeApprovals` rejects with `new Error("EACCES")` writes `Failed to update <path>: EACCES` to stderr.

routing.reasoning: Security-critical mass revocation, taint protection, confirmation ordering and lock-error mapping.

analysis: Existing TypeScript/Bun/Commander project; additive feature, no data migration. src/permissions/approvals-store.ts:19-24 documents byte-exact cache semantics; :26-46 defines ApprovalEntry and taint; :64-85 contains the existing isApprovalEntry and parseTaint parsing SSOT; :88-101 currently swallows all read/JSON errors and treats non-array entries as empty while retaining parsed taint. The new detailed read must distinguish missing from unparseable, count rejected array elements, and keep legacy read results wherever compatible; note the spec's unparseable-empty-taint rule conflicts with legacy taint preservation for an entries:string object, so prioritize explicit ACs and do not change valid-file behavior. src/permissions/approvals-store.ts:109-119 writes whole files and :121-139 serializes append under a path lock; removal must serialize read/decision/write using the same lock, preserve parsed taint, refuse unparseable input, and avoid creating the target on no-op. src/utils/path-file-lock.ts:27-38 delegates to a lock next to the file; src/utils/file-lock.ts:190-210 raises FILE_LOCK_TIMEOUT at 5s; account for absent parent directory when removing a missing store without creating a directory. src/permissions/approvals-taint.ts:51-67 provides isProcessAlive and :93-116 clears taint only on trusted runs; no CLI taint clearing. src/permissions/index.ts:3 already wildcard-exports store symbols, so new exports flow through the barrel. Existing dependent consumers include approvals-link, approvals-taint and ask-chain; regression suites test/unit/permissions/approvals-store.test.ts, approvals-link.test.ts, approvals-taint.test.ts protect existing cache behavior and taint safety. src/cli/runs.ts:14-19 derives config name or basename and calls projectOutputDir; src/runtime/paths.ts:19-34 maps project keys to ~/.nax and validates overrides; src/runtime/index.ts:319 uses the same project key. src/cli/auth.ts:1-25 establishes terminal-only CLI and injected logging/exit-code convention; src/cli/status-dispatch.ts:143-178 registers a Commander action and test/unit/cli/status-dispatch.test.ts:231 drives parseAsync. src/cli/confirm.ts:66-73 defaults to confirmation without a TTY, so the new CLI must check isTTY before invoking it. bin/nax.ts:1194-1230 groups auth and :1269 registers status; register approvals once nearby. docs/guides/cli-reference.md:1-65 is the CLI reference and docs/adr/ADR-030-bash-approval-modes.md:272 contains the trust-boundary section. New pure formatting module avoids the 600-line file gate; human output prints raw commands, JSON stays one stdout object even with warnings on stderr. IDs are computed SHA-256 over the three byte-exact fields and not persisted; identical triples may share IDs and are deleted together. Command functions return numeric exit status; registered actions call injected exit. Removal by id must validate all ids and find all matches inside locked decision, avoiding TOCTOU with concurrent append. --all checks empty before confirmation and refuses non-TTY without --yes. Work is split into six dependency-ordered stories matching the spec; existing file format, cache key and link remain unchanged.
outOfScope: `nax approvals add`, or any other way to create a remembered approval outside the human ask link.
Expiry, `--older-than`, or any time-based pruning of remembered approvals (D20: expiry NONE).
Id-prefix or partial-id matching in `nax approvals rm`; ids are exactly 8 hex characters.
Clearing or rewriting the approvals `taint` marker from the CLI; only a trusted run clears it through `clearApprovalsTaint`.
Masking or redacting secrets in `nax approvals list` output; commands print raw by ruling.
Any change to the `approvals.json` file format, the cache key, `findApproval`, `createApprovalsLink` or `approvals-taint.ts`.
A confirmation prompt for `rm <id...>` or `rm --stage`; revoking a grant can only cost prompts.
Refactoring the duplicated output-dir resolution in `src/cli/runs.ts` and `src/cli/status-cost.ts`.
